subject: English
passage: Radio broadcasting began reaching widespread audiences in the early twentieth century throughout North America and Europe, offering individuals unprecedented access to news, entertainment, and educational content from distant locations. This accessibility, combined with the relatively low cost of radio receivers, made radio immensely popular. Families could stay informed about world events, enjoy music and dramatic programs, and participate in educational programming from their homes. Radio listening quickly became a shared household activity, with communities organizing radio listening groups to experience these new forms of entertainment together.
prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: The low cost of radio receivers in the early twentieth century made it the preferred source of entertainment.
choices.B: The popularity of radio in the early twentieth century gave rise to the first community listening groups.
choices.C: The widespread broadcasting of radio in the early twentieth century made it more reliable for people to use.
choices.D: The widespread adoption of radio in the early twentieth century provided new opportunities for people.

explanation: Choice D is the best answer. The text discusses how widespread radio broadcasting in the early twentieth century allowed people to access distant content, stay informed about world events, enjoy entertainment programming, and participate in educational activities and community groups. All of these are new opportunities that were provided by the widespread adoption of radio.
